identity.fantasy: A two-handed demonic executioner who stacks wounds with Gore and Mutilation, changes Pestilence for the matchup, and cashes six stacks into Skulltaker.
identity.one_line: Build six wound or frenzy stacks, preserve Sever when its heal matters, then choose Skulltaker for immediate pressure or Meatsaw for sustained PvE payoff.

mechanics.core_loop: Apply Gore and the chosen wound tools, reach six stacks, and use Skulltaker; Pestilence and Unleash are adjusted for damage, healing or anti-heal needs.

mechanics.single_target: Skulltaker is the practical burst finisher; Meatsaw gains value when the target lives long enough for the channel or repeated damage.
mechanics.aoe: Bleeds, Burning Blade and cleaving finishers reward stable packs, though the loop remains more direct than Hellfire.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Mounted Combat, chains and snare tools help connect, but current PvP players say many classes can reapply slows or escape.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Hellborn self-healing, Sever and Unleash can be reserved for survival rather than spent automatically.
mechanics.group_utility: Pestilence can switch toward healing pressure or anti-heal, and chains create pickup utility.

failure_modes.text: Spending stacks on the wrong finisher loses either immediate kill pressure or durable-target value.
Using Sever or Unleash before incoming damage removes important self-healing.
Failing to swap Pestilence for a healer matchup wastes a core utility advantage.
